clue.text: Cargo for sailors, perhaps, and their leader

parts.note: shipmen is an old word for seamen; 'perhaps' marks it as one possible sailor word

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of 'their' is taken

explanation.surface: A crew's cargo, and their captain's too, seemingly loaded aboard together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their leader' gives T, tacked on after SHIPMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment of goods sent by sea or other transport is cargo.

clue.text: Plant employs Apache? It must be wrong!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are wrongly ordered and must be put right by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a plant could really make use of an Apache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be wrong' rearranges APACHE plus IT; 'employs' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatica is a low woodland flower of the buttercup family, liverwort, so a plant.

clue.text: Feature of BR non-stop progress at sea

parts.note: something non-stop is lasting, continuing without end
a ship under way is moving; way is a vessel's forward movement through water

explanation.surface: A slogan about British Rail running without stops while a ship pushes on.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the old UK national railway; the permanent way is its track bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway engineers call the laid track and its ballast the permanent way, a defining part of any rail network.

clue.text: Secret directions upsetting to schoolboy

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south

indicators.note: in a down clue to upset is to turn upside down, so the word 'to' is read bottom to top

parts.note: Eric is the schoolboy hero of the Victorian novel Eric, or Little by Little

explanation.surface: Hidden instructions that would distress a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsetting' turns 'to' bottom to top. Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, kept private like a secret.

clue.text: Italian city puts fresh heart into sad Parisian

indicators.note: 'puts ... into' says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: triste is the French word for sad, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of 'fresh'

explanation.surface: A city in Italy cheers up a gloomy Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh heart' is E, the middle of FRESH; 'into' places it inside TRISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a port city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic.

clue.text: "By the old Moulmein ——" (Kipling)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word completes the opening line of Kipling's poem Mandalay

explanation.surface: A line from Kipling with its last word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Mandalay opens 'By the old Moulmein Pagoda, lookin' lazy at the sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's opening line names a Burmese temple tower at Moulmein, which completes the quotation.

clue.text: She writes articles in two directions

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the article is written once forwards and once backwards, so it runs both ways

parts.note: a second article, the same word an

explanation.surface: A woman journalist composes pieces that point two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: AN forwards then backwards (NA) gives a name that reads the same both ways; 'writes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a woman, so it can replace the pronoun.

clue.text: She arranges material for oriental wear without sex-appeal

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the clothing word goes round the slang term

parts.note: to dress is to wear clothes; dress is also clothing
it is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A dressmaker dresses an Eastern client in something deliberately unalluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a female editor, who arranges written material for publication.

clue.text: Argued like one in debt

indicators.note: 'in' puts the comparison phrase inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means owing money, in debt
as means like, in the manner of
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone argued as though they owed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like one in debt' reads literally once 'like' is taken as the comparison word and debt as the red ink of an overdrawn account.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned case is one set out logically, as in a debate.

clue.text: More than one such incentive for a football team

definitions.text: More than one such incentive for a football team

parts.words: More than one such incentive for a football team
parts.note: read the plural of this goad as the nickname of Tottenham ..., the north London football club

explanation.surface: Bonuses offered to motivate footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club, is widely known as Spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A goad or stimulus to action, and its plural names a football club.

clue.text: Prosaic affair — cricket side take part

parts.note: a matter is an affair or business
the off side is one half of a cricket field
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A dull business: the cricket team plays its role.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter-of-fact means plain and unimaginative, like prose rather than poetry.

clue.text: Commander held arms fail if mishandled

indicators.note: the letters are handled badly and so jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Warning that held weapons may fail if treated carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if mishandled' rearranges HELD ARMS FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A field marshal is the highest rank of army officer, a supreme commander.

clue.text: Vet rears mongrel — makes us cross

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breeding, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A vet breeds a mutt, which annoys us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' mixes VET REARS; 'makes us' is a link, and 'cross' means go across, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a stretch of land is to go over it from side to side.

clue.text: Girl gets in German beer and cake for Angus

indicators.note: the girl gets inside the beer word

parts.note: bock is a strong German lager
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman enjoys a German lager and a Scottish treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angus' is a stock Scottish name, flagging a Scottish dish: a bannock is a flat round oatcake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish flat loaf or oatcake, a cake a Scot would eat.

clue.text: Was pressed to call?

parts.note: read as a description of a doorbell button, pushed by a caller to summon someone

explanation.surface: Someone was urged to make a phone call or visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A button pushed to ring a doorbell, which summons someone to the door.

clue.text: Poet gets across

explanation.surface: A poet manages to make himself understood.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges was an English poet laureate; spans that let traffic pass over a river do so.

clue.text: Witty answer to do with golfing terms

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with
par is the standard score for a golf hole
the tee is where each golf hole starts

explanation.surface: A clever reply involving the vocabulary of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, clever retort in conversation.

clue.text: They turn out to be adjustable covers, it appears

indicators.note: something adjustable can be rearranged, so these letters are reset

explanation.surface: Loose covers that seem able to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustable' rearranges COVERS IT; 'to be' and 'appears' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: People who throw tenants out of a property are said to turn them out.

clue.text: Many tormented become mad

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword shorthand for many
racked means tortured, tormented

explanation.surface: Lots of tortured people end up insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked is slang for crazy, someone who has gone mad.

clue.text: Finish of the main outing, as it were

definitions.text: Finish of the main outing, as it were

parts.words: Finish of the main outing, as it were
parts.note: the main is the sea; its going out is the tide ebbing, and its end is the lowest point of the ebb

explanation.surface: The end of the principal trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic word for the sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb tide at its lowest is when the sea has finished going out.

clue.text: Money once seen lying on the beach?

explanation.surface: Old coins spotted in the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was the old British sixpence, before decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pre-decimal sixpenny coin, and a sunbather browning on the sand.

clue.text: Calm mount backed by police

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the mountain word is read in reverse

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A peaceful horse supported by the constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ALP into PLA, followed by CID.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means quiet and untroubled, serene.

clue.text: They should be given a fair deal

definitions.text: They should be given a fair deal

parts.words: They should be given a fair deal
parts.note: read as a pack dealt honestly round the table, not people treated justly

explanation.surface: A plea for justice for some group.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is dealt out to players, and a fair deal is one without cheating.

clue.text: Annexes a cutter in the sound

indicators.note: the tool's name is spoken, not written

parts.note: an adze is a cutting tool like an axe with its blade at right angles

explanation.surface: Takes over a boat in a coastal channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a strait for the cutter (boat) to sail in, but it signals the spoken form.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex something is to add it, joining it on.

clue.text: Warning given by the more caring type?

definitions.text: Warning given by the more caring type?

parts.words: Warning given by the more caring type?
parts.note: a car horn's warning, and what someone who cares gives, from the idiom of not giving a damn

explanation.surface: An alert from a considerate person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not give a hoot' means not care at all, so a caring type gives one; a hoot is also a horn's warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A horn's blast warns others, and a caring person gives this from the idiom about caring.

clue.text: Africans make petition about Europeans

indicators.note: the petition word goes about, around, the Europeans

parts.note: to sue is to petition or plead
Danes are people of Denmark

explanation.surface: Africans lodge a complaint concerning people from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Sudan in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Fighter owed £2 — it's embarrassing

parts.note: due means owed
L is the pound sign's letter, so two pounds is two Ls

indicators.note: something embarrassed is put into disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A fighter is ashamed to owe a paltry two pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign comes from L for the Latin libra, so £2 is two Ls; 'embarrassing' rearranges 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist fights formal single combat with pistols or swords.
